title: converged fit on pixel-integral frames (one and seven sources) + retained point-sampled failure

frozen_inputs.frame: 9x9 TAN, CRVAL=(10,20) deg, CRPIX=(5,5), CD=0.001 deg/pix
frozen_inputs.positive_image: generated by evaluate_psf of a frozen EffectivePSF with sigma=1.2 (the same pixel-integral model as the fitter), unit total flux 100
frozen_inputs.retained_image: point-sampled Gaussian at pixel centres (outside the model family)
frozen_inputs.fit: gaussian family, spatial degree 0, window radius 3, tolerance 1e-8 / 512 iterations
frozen_inputs.seven_source_case: 7 sources at (2,2),(4,6),(6,3),(7,7),(2,7),(6,6),(4,2) in the same 9x9 frame, sigma=1.35, fluxes 6722..4400, one shared spatial degree - the x01-00 shape
frozen_inputs.m6_regression: the seven-source case fails on the pre-fix Jacobian (position/shape columns missing the source flux) with nonconverged and passes after the factor is restored

diagnosis: the original x01 failure was a Jacobian defect: the model is flux * template, but the position and shape columns of the Jacobian were built from template derivatives without the source flux. In x01-00 the flux is about 6722, so those columns were too small by that factor: the trust region shrank the step by about 1.8e-3, the predicted reduction (2.07) disagreed with the true gradient dot (2269), and the Armijo line search could not find a decreasing trial. Multiplying both blocks by the source flux restores the exact Gauss-Newton direction; the point-sampled frame stays a model-family mismatch and is retained as a named failure.
